## The decision this serves

Your figure has 22 cell types in a rainbow palette and your co-author cannot read it. Decide what the figure is actually for.

::: {.callout-important}
**Scale.** Runs in 3 min, peak memory under 2 GB.
Watch **category count, past about eight** — that is what stops being safe on a full section.
:::

## Concept

Equal aspect ratio, scale bars in microns, one hue for continuous quantities, and the readable ceiling of about eight categorical colours.

**The assumption that breaks first.** That a palette which looks fine on your monitor is readable to your readers.

## Failure mode

**What it produces.** A rainbow scale invents boundaries that are not in the data, and twenty categories at once hide the pattern the figure was meant to show.

**The diagnostic that catches it.** Render the palette through a colour-vision deficiency simulation and compute the distances rather than eyeballing them.
